trace.code: s->virtual_disk_size = le64_to_cpu(s->virtual_disk_size);  // read straight from image metadata; pre-fix there is NO VHDX_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE (64 TiB) bound here (the fix inserts the check at line 818)
data_blocks_cnt = DIV_ROUND_UP(s->virtual_disk_size, s->block_size);  // uint32_t data_blocks_cnt: a >4 PiB size truncates (2^32+1 blocks -> 1)
s->bat_entries = data_blocks_cnt + ((data_blocks_cnt - 1) >> s->chunk_ratio_bits);  // BAT undersized relative to total_sectors
bs->total_sectors = s->virtual_disk_size >> s->logical_sector_size_bits;  // total_sectors uses the FULL 64-bit size (~2^46), so high sectors stay 'valid'

sinfo->bat_idx = sector_num >> s->sectors_per_block_bits; ... sinfo->file_offset = s->bat[sinfo->bat_idx] & VHDX_BAT_FILE_OFF_MASK;  // NO bounds check on bat_idx (pre-fix); the fix adds assert(sinfo->bat_idx < s->bat_entries) at 1157

s->bat[sinfo->bat_idx] |= state & VHDX_BAT_STATE_BIT_MASK;  // write path (vhdx_update_bat_table_entry) — but unreachable past the allocation: vhdx_co_writev calls vhdx_block_translate FIRST, whose OOB READ at line 1152 crashes before this write executes

preconditions: A malicious VHDX disk image whose 'Virtual Disk Size' metadata item is set to a size > 4 PiB (2^55+2^23) with a 8 MiB block size, so the uint32 block count wraps to 1

The image is opened by any QEMU tool (qemu-img info/convert/map/check, qemu-io, qemu-storage-daemon, or attached as a VM disk) — no privilege on the QEMU host beyond the ability to supply the image (cloud image-import pipelines, shared VM images, or a user running qemu-img locally)
A read or write at a high-but-in-range offset (>= 1 TiB) is issued — trivially reached by a guest on a >4 PiB virtual disk, or by qemu-io/qemu-img dd directly

evidence.vulnerable_version: QEMU <= 11.1.3 (and Debian 10.0.13 qemu-img/qemu-io) — virtual_disk_size unvalidated, no bat_idx bounds check. Present since VHDX support (QEMU 2.0).
evidence.fixed_version: unreleased on master (11.2.0-dev @ 67198583, 2026-10-23); NOT backported to stable-11.1 as of 2026-11-12 (stable-11.1 last touched block/vhdx.c 2025-09-15)
evidence.observed_result: Driving the REAL qemu-img 10.0.13 / qemu-io binary: qemu-img info accepts a VHDX patched to 'virtual size: 32 PiB' (no VHDX_MAX_IMAGE_SIZE bound). CONTROL (unpatched 1 MiB image): read@0 succeeds, read@1PiB returns a clean 'read failed: Input/output error'. EXPLOIT (patched image): qemu-io read AND write at offset 1 PiB both die with SIGSEGV (exit 139) — the bat_idx = 2^27 runs far past the ~1 MiB BAT allocation (bat_entries=1). Both crashes are the OOB READ in vhdx_block_translate (the masked read result becomes a file offset, so no host bytes are disclosed; the write-path OOB store is unreachable because the read crashes first). Honest impact = host/VM crash (DoS), A:H only. Marker printed: QEMUOVERRUN-OK / Segmentation fault.

real_exploit.target: qemu 10.0.13 (Debian 13 qemu-img + qemu-io) — the real block/vhdx.c BAT translation code in the shipped binary, driven against a crafted VHDX
real_exploit.backend: qemu-img / qemu-io (real QEMU binaries) opening and I/O-driving the patched VHDX; make_vhdx.py crafts the malicious image by patching the real 'Virtual Disk Size' metadata item
real_exploit.demonstrated: qemu-img info reports a 32 PiB virtual disk (missing size bound), and qemu-io SIGSEGVs (exit 139) on BOTH read and write at a 1 PiB offset — the unchecked bat_idx (2^27) reads far past the 1-entry BAT heap allocation. The unpatched 1 MiB control image errors cleanly at the same offset, proving the crash is caused by the oversized virtual_disk_size, not by the offset itself. Impact demonstrated = host/VM crash (DoS, A:H); the OOB read result is masked to a file offset (no host-memory disclosure, C:N) and the OOB write is unreachable (the read crashes first, I:N).

evidence.notes: No public CVE/GHSA assigned as of 2026-11-12 (upstream tracks it under QEMU work_items 3762/4470/4487/4638/4733; reported independently by Palo Alto Networks, Calif.io, Xiang Chen, Daniel Wade, Mayank Jangid, Ken Hsu/Royce Lu/Bo Qu). The commit message confirms 'out-of-bounds access on the BAT array from both the read and write paths'. Fix is in master + v11.2.0-rc0 (commit 67198583, merged 2026-11-09); NOT backported to stable-11.1 (still vulnerable on the stable line). Palo Alto's independent assessment of the same bug rates it 5.5 MEDIUM (AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) — DoS only; we follow that.
